finding.title: Unauthenticated /metrics renders O(N) attacker-inflated stats while holding the same mutex every gateway request takes -> lock starvation
finding.evidence: /metrics has no auth by explicit design - routes.go:19-24: `// ... 故不做 JWT 鉴权` followed by `r.GET("/metrics", func(c *gin.Context) {` ... `s.mx.WritePromRender(c.Writer, s)`. The render path takes a lock and iterates the whole stats map while holding it: metrics.go:88-100 `func (mt *Metrics) QPS() []QPSInfo {` / `mt.mu.Lock()` / `defer mt.mu.Unlock()` / `for m, s := range mt.stats {` / `s.rotate(time.Now().Unix())` ... (rotate at metrics.go:16-33 does up to 59 iterations of two 60-element array copies). That same `mt.mu` is the mutex every gateway request takes at least three times: metrics.go:114 `func (mt *Metrics) ConnInc() { mt.mu.Lock(); mt.conns++; mt.mu.Unlock() }`, 115-121 ConnDec, 122 `func (mt *Metrics) Conns() int64 { mt.mu.Lock(); ...`, plus Observe/RecordError - reached from gateway.go:195 (`int64(snap.General.MaxConnections) > 0 && s.mx.Conns() >= int64(snap.General.MaxConnections)`), gateway.go:300-301 and gateway.go:318. prom.go:112-114 (`func (mt *Metrics) WritePromRender(...) { mt.promMu.Lock(); defer mt.promMu.Unlock()`) only serializes scrapes; it does not shorten the mt.mu hold, and each queued scrape keeps its handler goroutine + connection alive. prom.go:135-139 emits HELP+TYPE+sample twice per key, so the response body is O(N x len(key)) too. Extra evidence that N is reachable from the inside: dashboard/status calls the same O(N) render from an authenticated poll that the shipped SPA runs every 5s (backend/internal/admin/dashboard.go:137 `"qps_by_model":  s.mx.QPS(),` with frontend/src/pages/settings/RuntimeStatus.tsx:34 `refetchInterval: 5000,`).
finding.impact: dos-1 gives an attacker a permanent, cheap knob for N. A single unauthenticated client then loops `GET /metrics` (no key, no rate limit, no connection cap on this route since MaxConnections is only counted inside Handle) and holds `mt.mu` for O(N) each time. At N = 10^5 stale keys the hold is tens of milliseconds per scrape, which at scrape-per-response loop rate is a ~100% duty cycle on the global mutex, so *every* gateway request blocks in ConnInc/Conns/Observe: the whole data plane stalls to a crawl while the process looks healthy (CPU low, no errors). Concurrently, /metrics responses themselves become multi-MB (26 MB+ at 100k x 30-byte keys), and because no server read/write deadline exists (dos-4) a slow-reading scraper pins handler goroutines and sockets indefinitely -> goroutine/fd pileup. Also leaks the entire historical model namespace (including private/implicit upstream model names used as keys) to unauthenticated callers.
finding.recommendation: Decouple the render lock from the collection lock: take mt.mu only to snapshot (m, total, errs) into a slice, release, then format. Give QPS() a hard output cap (top-K by QPS plus an aggregate bucket) and skip entries whose 60s windows are all zero. Add a cardinality ceiling on Prometheus label values (truncate to e.g. 64 bytes) so response size cannot be inflated. Require a token/mTLS or at minimum bind /metrics to an internal interface, and add a per-endpoint concurrency limit / ReadHeaderTimeout so scrapes cannot pile up.
finding.mitigations_checked: promMu serializes scrapes (prom.go:113) but this *increases* goroutine pileup rather than bounding it; rotate() self-clears when shift >= 60 (metrics.go:21-23) so old windows read zero - that makes eviction safe but does not free the entry; TRUSTED_PROXIES/XFF is irrelevant here (no IP-based control on /metrics at all); the endpoint is a plain text writer with no body reading, so no inbound-size limit applies.

reason:
DOWNGRADE high -> medium. Every cited quote is verbatim-accurate and the structural coupling the filer describes is real, but the load-bearing severity claim - "~100% duty cycle on the global mutex, so *every* gateway request blocks ... the whole data plane stalls to a crawl" - is contradicted by direct measurement of the exact code path: the achievable mt.mu duty cycle from /metrics saturates at ~5-6% and is INDEPENDENT of N, so no amount of inflation turns this into starvation. What survives is a genuine but bounded unauthenticated availability + disclosure primitive, i.e. medium (defense-in-depth gap with real impact), not the "data plane stalls to a crawl" high.

=== 1. QUOTE / LINE VERIFICATION (all files read end-to-end; filed line numbers are correct, so corrected_line stays 88) ===
(a) metrics.go:88 is exactly `func (mt *Metrics) QPS() []QPSInfo {`; 89 `mt.mu.Lock()`; 90 `defer mt.mu.Unlock()`; 92 `for m, s := range mt.stats {`; 93 `s.rotate(time.Now().Unix())`; 95-98 the two 60-element sums; 101 `sort.Slice(...)` INSIDE the same hold; 102 return. The whole O(N) walk + sort is under mt.mu with no yield. Confirmed. metrics.go:16-33 rotate is as quoted (shift<60 does up to 59 iterations of two 60-element copies; for stale attacker keys shift>=60 takes the 960-byte zeroing branch at 21-23 - measured indistinguishable: 18.67 ms stale vs 18.92 ms fresh at N=100k).
(b) metrics.go:114/115-121/122 ConnInc/ConnDec/Conns are verbatim as quoted, all on the SAME mt.mu (field declared at metrics.go:42). Observe (56-71) and RecordError (73-80) also on mt.mu.
(c) Gateway side confirmed: gateway.go:195 `if int64(snap.General.MaxConnections) > 0 && s.mx.Conns() >= int64(snap.General.MaxConnections) {` inside AuthMiddleware; gateway.go:300 `s.mx.ConnInc()`; 301 `defer s.mx.ConnDec()`; 318 `s.mx.Observe(ap.alias, ap.status != "ok")`. MaxConnections DEFAULTS TO 1000 (settings.go:32 `MaxConnections: 1000, GuardEnabled: true, ...`), so the Conns() probe is live by default => a gateway request takes mt.mu FOUR times by default (Conns, ConnInc, ConnDec, Observe), which is if anything understated by the filer's "at least three".
(d) routes.go:19-24 confirmed: line 20 is the comment `// （LB/网关层限制），故不做 JWT 鉴权——鉴权会让抓取端无法简单配置。`, line 21 `r.GET("/metrics", func(c *gin.Context) {`, line 23 `s.mx.WritePromRender(c.Writer, s)`. The handler is registered on the bare engine (before the /v1 group that gets `gw.Use(gws.AuthMiddleware())` at routes.go:28), so it is unauthenticated, unthrottled and takes no gin middleware beyond Recovery/headers/access-log (main.go:95-118). "Bind to internal interface" is advisory only: main.go:126 `srv := &http.Server{Addr: fmt.Sprintf(":%d", cfg.ListenPort), Handler: engine}` binds all interfaces and there is no ListenHost/METRICS_TOKEN anywhere in the backend (grep for ListenHost|BIND|METRICS_TOKEN|127.0.0.1: only tests + port). No per-route connection cap either - ConnInc happens only inside Handle, so /metrics traffic never counts against MaxConnections. All correct as filed.
(e) The render really does call the O(N) collector: prom.go:113-114 takes promMu, prom.go:118 `snap = col.PromSnapshot()`, and admin/prom.go:14-16 `if s.mx != nil { snap.ModelQPS = s.mx.QPS() }` - i.e. exactly one mt.mu hold per scrape, taken WHILE promMu is held. prom.go:120-123 fallback is not reached in production. prom.go:135-139 emits two labelled metrics per key, each preceded by HELP+TYPE (writeMetric at prom.go:48-58), so the body is ~345 B + 2*len(key) per key. prom.go:112-114 quoted accurately; the filer's own remark that promMu "does not shorten the mt.mu hold" is right about length but wrong about its consequence (see 3).
(f) Secondary citations verified: dashboard.go:137 `"qps_by_model":  s.mx.QPS(),` (inside `func (s *Server) status`, routes.go:142 behind s.AuthMiddleware()) and frontend/src/pages/settings/RuntimeStatus.tsx:34 `refetchInterval: 5000,` for queryKey ['runtime-status'] -> runtimeStatusApi.get() = GET /status. Accurate, but note that path is authenticated, so it is not an attacker lever - it only shows the same O(N) hold is already being paid by the console every 5s.
(g) Permanence verified: metrics.go has no delete/cap/TTL on mt.stats (only writers are New():53 and Observe():63; grep for `delete(` in metrics.go = 0 hits) and mx is constructed once (main.go:65) and never recreated on hot reload, so N is a monotonic high-water mark. Consistent with the sibling verification of dos-1 (docs/security/raw/verify-dos-1.json = confirmed/high), so I accept N's reachability as established and do not re-litigate it here - except to record that dos-1's own exploit_sketch already claims this exact /metrics step as its step 3, so dos-2 is largely the same primitive priced a second time.

=== 2. MEASUREMENT (why the impact statement fails) ===
I ran the file's own code - ModelStat/rotate/QPS/ConnInc/Conns copied verbatim from metrics.go plus the per-key emit loop from prom.go:135-139 - in a throwaway module under %TEMP%\verifydos2 (no repo file was created or modified), on go1.24.4 windows/amd64, GOMAXPROCS=12, keys ~30 B:
  N=1e3    QPS() hold 0.10 ms    render 4.1 ms     body 0.33 MB
  N=1e4    QPS() hold 1.6  ms    render 31  ms     body 3.3  MB
  N=1e5    QPS() hold 18.7 ms    render 347 ms     body 33.1 MB
Then I drove a 64-goroutine synthetic data plane (3 mt.mu acquires per request, mirroring gateway.go:195/300/318) for a 4 s window while N=1e5, with 0/1/8/24 concurrent unauthenticated /metrics loops:
  clients=0  : mean wait 0s      p99 0s      max 120 us   >1ms  0.0%  duty 0.4%
  clients=1  : mean wait 280 us  p99 17.5 ms max 20.5 ms  >1ms  2.2%  duty 5.4%  (2.8 scrapes/s)
  clients=8  : mean wait 650 us  p99 24   ms max 24   ms  >1ms  5.4%  duty 5.7%  (2.2 scrapes/s)
  clients=24 : mean wait 1.28 ms p99 31   ms max 31   ms  >1ms  6.5%  duty 6.4%  (2.0 scrapes/s)
Two things kill the filed impact. FIRST, the hold is ~18.7 ms but the render is ~347 ms and happens OUTSIDE mt.mu, so one scrape cycle holds the collection lock only ~5% of its own wall time - "tens of milliseconds" per scrape is right, "~100% duty cycle" is off by ~20x. SECOND, adding clients does not raise duty at all (5.4% -> 6.4% from 1 to 24 scrapers) precisely BECAUSE of promMu (prom.go:113): holds cannot overlap, extra scrapers just queue. And because hold and render are both Theta(N), the ratio - hence the duty ceiling - does not improve for the attacker as N grows: at N=1e6 the extrapolated hold is ~190 ms against a ~3.5 s render, still ~5%. The mutex therefore has a hard ~6% ceiling on this route; the correct statement of the harm is "up to ~20-30 ms of added latency on ~2-6% of gateway requests, plus ~0.35 s of CPU and ~33 MB of egress per scrape", not a stalled data plane. (The CPU/egress cost is real - 24 scrapers saturate the box's cores and 298 MB egress in 4 s - but that is generic unauthenticated O(N)-work-per-request amplification, not lock starvation, and each request still completes.)
Also note the filer's premise "the process looks healthy (CPU low, no errors)" is self-defeating: 33 MB of fmt.Fprintf per scrape is high CPU, which is exactly what a defender's own /metrics + node alerting sees, and the same scrape stream is recorded by the access log (main.go:106-118) with client IP.

=== 3. WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE AND WORTH KEEPING (the residual, medium) ===
(i) Coupling exists: an unauthenticated route acquires a mutex that every gateway request must acquire 4x by default; worst-case single-request stall measured at 20-31 ms at N=1e5 and growing linearly with N (the per-EVENT harm does scale with N even though duty does not). Latency inflation, not denial.
(ii) promMu is a genuine single-point hazard the filer half-saw: because the O(N) write happens under promMu (prom.go:113) and http.Server has no Read/Write/Idle deadlines (main.go:126, WriteTimeout=0 by design), ONE connection that reads a 33 MB body slowly parks every other scrape indefinitely (measured scrape_cycle_max 3.74 s/3.95 s with 8/24 clients = queueing behind a single render; unbounded if the reader stalls). That degrades/blinds monitoring - the operator's outage-detection path - at zero CPU cost to the attacker. Real, unauthenticated, cheap; it does not touch the data plane.
(iii) Unauthenticated information disclosure: prom.go:136 `l := `model="` + promEsc(q.Model) + `"`` prints every key ever observed by Observe, and those keys are raw client-supplied model strings (gateway.go:334) - so /metrics hands any unauthenticated caller the full historical model namespace, configured aliases plus implicit upstream model names (gateway.go:351 path), with no eviction. That is a concrete, unauthenticated confidentiality regression beyond the "no auth on /metrics" architecture fact, and by itself justifies keeping this finding open.
(iv) The recommendation is technically sound and cheap (snapshot-under-lock then format; skip all-zero windows; cap label cardinality; token-bind or split-port /metrics). The snapshot-then-format fix alone converts a Theta(N) critical section into a Theta(N) off-lock copy and a Theta(1) map walk... strictly it is still Theta(N) under the lock, so I would add the cardinality/zero-skip bound as the real fix.

=== 4. MITIGATIONS I CHECKED AND DID NOT FIND ===
No auth, no token, no IP allowlist, no concurrency limit, no rate limit, no per-route timeout on /metrics (routes.go:21, main.go:92-126); no eviction or size cap on mt.stats (metrics.go:41-71); no zero-window skip and no output cap in QPS()/prom render (metrics.go:88-103, prom.go:135-139); no write-error handling in writeMetric (prom.go:48-58), so a disconnected scraper's handler still finishes the whole O(N) loop. TRUSTED_PROXIES is irrelevant (no IP control here at all), as the filer said. The only partial mitigation is the one the filer dismissed - promMu - and it does bound concurrency of the hold to exactly 1, which is the single most important number in this re-review and the reason for the downgrade.
exploit_sketch:
Prerequisite for the amplification factor is dos-1's N (one valid enabled gateway key; ~100k cheap 404s `POST /v1/chat/completions {"model":"zz-<i>"}` -> permanent mt.stats entries, metrics.go:63). The /metrics side itself needs NO credential and NO rate limit.

A) Lock-contention latency inflation (bounded, ~6% duty - NOT a stall):
  while :; do curl -s -o /dev/null http://target:8080/metrics; done
Measured at N=1e5: 18.7 ms hold per scrape, ~347 ms render per scrape, duty 5.4%; 2-6% of concurrent gateway requests' ConnInc/Conns/Observe acquisitions block past 1 ms, p99 added latency 17-31 ms. Scale to 24 parallel loops: duty 6.4% (promMu at prom.go:113 forbids overlap), so the data plane degrades by ~30 ms tails and ~0.35 s of core-time per scrape, not a crawl. N=1e6 (~1 GB map) would put the per-event stall at ~190 ms.

B) Monitoring blindness + goroutine/socket pileup (cheapest real unauth hit, 0 CPU):
  python3 -c "import socket;s=socket.create_connection(('target',8080));s.sendall(b'GET /metrics HTTP/1.1\r\nHost:x\r\n\r\n');import time;time.sleep(10**6)"
One connection that never drains the 33 MB body pins the render inside promMu (prom.go:113-114) forever - no WriteTimeout (main.go:126) and writeMetric ignores write errors (prom.go:48-58) - so every legitimate Prometheus/VictoriaMetrics scrape queues behind it indefinitely and operators lose the metrics path during the exact window they would be investigating the latency from (A).

C) Unauthenticated namespace disclosure (works at default N, no dos-1 needed):
  curl -s http://target:8080/metrics | grep -o 'model="[^"]*"' | sort -u
Every model string ever requested is echoed as a label value (prom.go:136-138) and never evicted, exposing private aliases and implicit upstream model names to any unauthenticated network client.
